claim.quote: No new physics signal is observed, and we set world-leading limits on heavy QCD axions, as well as for the Higgs portal scalar among dedicated searches.

date.quote: Search for a Hidden Sector Scalar from Kaon Decay in the Di-Muon Final State at ICARUS

key_value_text.quote: The search is performed with data collected in the Neutrinos at the Main Injector (NuMI) beam at Fermilab corresponding to 2.41×10²⁰ protons-on-target.
key_value_text.value: World-leading exclusion limits on heavy QCD axions and on a Higgs-portal scalar produced in kaon decay and decaying to two muons, from 2.41×10²⁰ protons-on-target in the NuMI beam; no long-lived-particle signal observed

name: Search for a Hidden Sector Scalar from Kaon Decay in the Di-Muon Final State at ICARUS
notes: This is ICARUS's first published physics result from its Fermilab SBN run (data taking began 5 November 2021); it uses the off-axis NuMI beam rather than the on-axis BNB beam used for the sterile-neutrino search.

significance.locator: arXiv:2411.02727, abstract (no significance/sigma reported for a null result)
significance.note: An exclusion-limit search: no signal was observed.

summary.plain: Using its new home at Fermilab, ICARUS looked for a hidden new particle that could pop out of kaon decays and turn into two muons. It didn't find one, but that let it rule out a wide range of possible hidden particles.
summary.technical: Search for long-lived hidden-sector particles (heavy QCD axions, Higgs-portal scalars) produced in K -> pi + LLP decays and decaying to mu+mu- inside ICARUS-T600, using 2.41x10^20 POT from the off-axis NuMI beam at Fermilab. No signal observed; sets world-leading limits among dedicated searches for these two models.

title: Search for a Hidden Sector Scalar from Kaon Decay in the Di-Muon Final State at ICARUS
why_it_matters: This is ICARUS's first published physics result since its move to Fermilab, demonstrating the refurbished T600's ability to search for physics beyond sterile neutrinos (hidden-sector long-lived particles) using the NuMI beam in addition to its primary BNB-based sterile-neutrino programme.
